solutions.latex:
$$\dfrac{\sin B}{1260} = \dfrac{\sin 40^\circ 21'}{880} \quad\therefore\quad B = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sin 40^\circ 21'}{880} \times 1260\right) = 67^\circ 59'$$

$$\text{Angle } A = 180^\circ - 67^\circ 59' - 40^\circ 21' = 71^\circ 40'$$

Angle $A$: $71^\circ 40'$; Angle $B$: $67^\circ 59'$; Angle $C$: $40^\circ 21'$; Side $a$: $1290$ m; Side $b$: $1260$ m; Side $c$: $880$ m.

$$\text{time taken} = \dfrac{1000\text{ kJ}}{(7000 \div 24)} \div 4 = 51 \text{ mins } 26 \text{ seconds}$$

$$\text{Total distance} = \dfrac{16}{60} \times 51 \text{ mins } 26 \text{ seconds} = 13.71 \text{ km}$$

2 km loops therefore $7$ laps needed.

notes: Mathematics Standard 2, William Clarke College, Year 12 Assessment Task 1. Cover prints 2022 and date 24/11/2022 (Term 4 of Year 11), so graduation year 2023 used. Bundled handwritten-marked solutions (scan, pages 20-35) transcribed from images; Q2 answers marked 'Answers May Vary'; Q3c has no printed mark breakdown.
